clue.text: Turncoat Frenchman keeping old oath

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the Frenchman's name wraps round the oath

parts.note: Rene is a typical French man's name
egad is an archaic mild oath, a softened 'by God'

explanation.surface: A French traitor is caught still clinging to an outdated vow of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old oath' signals a dated exclamation from period novels, the kind of mild curse crosswords love; 'keeping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter who switches sides, especially abandoning a cause or faith, is a direct synonym of a turncoat.

clue.text: Signal transmitted in the wrong order

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase for transmitted change places, a front-to-back shift of letters

parts.note: to put out a programme or statement is to transmit or broadcast it

explanation.surface: A message got broadcast with its parts jumbled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wrong order' swaps the halves of PUT OUT, bringing OUT to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In electronics the signal leaving a device, as from an amplifier, is its produced signal; the word names that delivered signal.

clue.text: Union in part of London is unfriendly towards the north

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
in puts the unfriendly word inside the district

parts.note: Kew is a district of south-west London, home of the botanic gardens
cold means distant and unfriendly

explanation.surface: A marriage in a London district has turned frosty in a northerly direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew is a district of south-west London, home of the botanic gardens. 'towards the north' turns the whole container result upward, as this is a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The marriage state is a union of two people, so marriage is a straightforward synonym here.

clue.text: Save wayward ladies, indeed, following admission

indicators.note: after being admitted, i.e. let inside, the affirmative sits within the reworked letters
wayward means wilful and unruly, so these letters go astray into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
ay is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to rescue errant women, once they have been let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wayward' rearranges the fodder so the affirmative can be let in after its first letter; 'Save' is a verb, as in setting money by.
explanation.definitionFit: To put money by for later is to keep or reserve it, the saving sense of save.

clue.text: Complaint primarily about Greek meal sent back with cold filling

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the cold letter sits within the reversed meal
sent back means the letters of the meal run in reverse in a down clue

parts.note: meze is a Greek spread of small appetiser dishes
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of about is used

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles about a Greek meal that was returned because it came out cold inside.
explanation.walkthrough: MEZE 'sent back' gives EZEM; C 'filling' it gives ECZEM, then 'primarily about' adds A.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an ailment or disorder, and this itchy skin inflammation is one such condition.

clue.text: Compliant lie dying following attack?

indicators.note: after an attack things are left battered and disordered, so these letters are knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone lies submissively, dying after being assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following attack?' shuffles LIE DYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ready to give way or submit to others is the same as being compliant; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Plan to escape on retiring after school

indicators.note: after places the reversed escape word behind the school abbreviation
retiring means drawing back, so the word for escape is read backwards

parts.note: to elude is to escape or evade

explanation.surface: A pupil hatches a plan to run away once they retire after lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like going to bed but tells you to read the escape word backwards; 'to' and 'on' are just link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable of intended events is a plan; the two words are synonyms as nouns and verbs.

clue.text: Letters from Athens dictated somewhere in Africa

indicators.note: dictated means spoken out for someone to write down, so the letters are heard rather than seen

parts.note: chi and rho are two letters of the Greek alphabet, said together like 'ki-ro'

explanation.surface: Correspondence from Greece was read out to someone on the African continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, the Greek letters chi and rho sound like the Egyptian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Egypt is a city on the Nile, so it is indeed a place within the African continent.

clue.text: Frozen cape toured by lorry

indicators.note: toured by means having something travel round it, so the lorry word surrounds the cape letter

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large truck in British usage
C is a standard abbreviation for cape on maps

explanation.surface: An icy headland is driven round by a big truck.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC, British slang for an articulated lorry (a semi-trailer truck), goes round C.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar regions are bitterly cold, so the adjective describing them means extremely cold or frozen.

clue.text: At an end after large amount of money crashes?

definitions.note: plural clue word against a singular answer: one such event involves several crashes, hence the question mark

indicators.note: after puts the end phrase behind the money word

parts.note: a pile is a fortune, as in 'make a pile'
up means finished, as in 'time is up'

explanation.surface: Money runs out once a fortune collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes' looks like a verb about stock markets but is the definition: a multiple collision.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-vehicle collision on a road is a series of crashes happening together, hence the hinted plural.

clue.text: Welsh town girl overwhelmed by backing of everybody without exception?

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped or surrounded, so the girl sits inside the other letters
backing means going in reverse, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: the phrase 'one and all' means everybody without exception, giving I for one plus ALL
Nell is a girl's name, short for Eleanor or Helen

explanation.surface: A young woman is swept away by the support of an entire Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'everybody without exception' as 'one and all': I + ALL, which 'backing of' turns to LLAI, round NELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Carmarthenshire, south Wales, famous for rugby and tinplate, fits the Welsh-town definition.

clue.text: Unrealistic novel by jerk

parts.note: roman is the French word for a novel, used in English in roman a clef
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a book by a fool as fanciful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests an idiot author, but it is a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealised or fanciful, rather than practical, is a common sense of this adjective, making it a synonym of unrealistic.

clue.text: Tax department so far gathering intelligence about foreigners

parts.note: IR is the Inland Revenue, the former British tax department

indicators.note: gathering means collecting into itself, so the outer word surrounds the reversed intelligence

parts.note: as is used for so far as, in the sense of to the extent that

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the intelligence letters are reversed

parts.note: IQ is the intelligence quotient, a measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: The taxman has so far been collecting intelligence on overseas nationals.
explanation.walkthrough: IR is the old British Inland Revenue. IQ turned 'about' gives QI, which AS is 'gathering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of a particular Middle Eastern country are foreigners from a British viewpoint; the definition is a broad category containing them.

clue.text: Keeping pace with a depraved guy who's run to hide

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so the brute contains the run letter

parts.note: a beast is a cruel or depraved man
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner stays level with a nasty fellow who has fled to go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAST takes in R, giving BREAST, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level and alongside someone, side by side, is to keep up with them, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Order and combine networked browsers?

parts.note: to book something is to order or reserve it
to club together is to combine resources

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort and merge web browsers on a computer network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'browsers' suggests web software, but means people who leaf through books; 'networked' means linked in a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading society links people who browse volumes, a playful description of members of such a group.

clue.text: Around hotel, salesmen knocked back drink

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the reversed salesmen surround the hotel name
knocked back means returned, so the letters for salesmen run backwards

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a famous luxury hotel in London

explanation.surface: Travelling salesmen gathered round a hotel and downed their drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking, but it reverses the salesmen. The Ritz is a famous London hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine mixed with soda water is a kind of drink, so the definition is a broad category.

clue.text: Shadow leaves tigers partially obscured

indicators.note: partially obscured means only part is visible, so the answer lies inside the words

explanation.surface: Foliage half-hides big cats lurking in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: It runs through leaVES TIGErs.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint trace or remnant can be called a shadow, as in 'a shadow of its former self'; the noun senses match.

clue.text: Tragic husband wearing naughty panties

indicators.note: the scrambled garment is worn by the husband letter, so it goes round that letter
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A sorry spectacle: a married man caught wearing saucy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' shuffles the underwear before 'wearing' wraps it round the husband. 'Tragic' here means relating to stage tragedy, an adjectival use.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to drama and the stage, as tragedy does; the adjective describes theatrical acting, so tragic fits loosely.

clue.text: 50% of Disney finally linked with business in a state

indicators.note: the final letter of the half-name is linked into the business word, joining it after its first letter
half of the six letters are dropped, keeping the second three

parts.note: work means business or trade

explanation.surface: Half of Disney is finally tied up with a company somewhere in America.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% of' leaves NEY; with WORK, its final Y 'linked with' WORK goes into it: NE + W(Y)ORK.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the fifty US states lies in the north-east; the definition names the category it belongs to.

clue.text: Tanker was emptied in the name of war

indicators.note: in places the emptied word inside the war name

parts.note: the Boer War was fought in South Africa between Britain and the Boer republics

indicators.note: emptied means the middle is removed, leaving just the outside letters

explanation.surface: An oil tanker was drained in the cause of war.
explanation.walkthrough: WS ('was emptied') goes 'in' BOER, the name of the Boer War. A bowser is a British word for a tanker truck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile tank for water or fuel, especially a truck refuelling aircraft, is a kind of tanker.

clue.text: Food is turning, affected internally

indicators.note: internally means inside, so the affected word goes within
turning means reversing direction, so the two letters run backwards

parts.note: camp means theatrically affected

explanation.surface: Food is going off, causing an internal upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' suggests illness but means theatrically mannered; 'turning' looks like food spoiling but is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded fried langoustines are a dish, so they are an example of food.

clue.text: Brains required where soldiers go in?

definitions.meaning: soldiers are strips of toast dipped into soft-boiled eggs, through the tops

explanation.surface: Clever planners are needed to decide where troops should attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldiers' are not troops but toast fingers, a British breakfast dipped into a boiled egg's top.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellectuals and clever people are informally called brains; the two are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Heavenly pair of legs exposed when lifting short skirt

indicators.note: lifting means raising, so in a down clue the letters run upwards
exposed means stripped of the outer covering, so the outer letters go

parts.note: a miniskirt, or mini, is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A lovely pair of legs is shown off as a brief skirt rides up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips LEGS to EG, which 'lifting' turns to GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Twins constellation, Castor and Pollux, is a pair of stars in the sky, hence heavenly.

clue.text: Tight knot finally loosened up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the letters reverse

parts.note: a knur is a knot or hard lump in wood

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A tight knot finally comes undone.
explanation.walkthrough: KNUR + D read 'up' the grid gives the answer. 'Tight' looks like part of the picture but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is informal slang for intoxicated, so a synonym of inebriated.

clue.text: He tried to sink many reds in match finals in BBC one-day snooker broadcast

definitions.text: He tried to sink many reds

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: finals means the last letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A snooker player tried to pot lots of red balls in a televised one-day final.
explanation.walkthrough: MATCH plus C, Y, R ('finals in' BBC, one-day, snooker) are 'broadcast'. 'reds' are Communists, not snooker balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The US senator hunted suspected Communists in the 1950s, trying to bring down Reds, hence the snooker pun.

clue.text: Plan work with head of admin to stop corporation in recession

indicators.note: in recession means moving back, so the whole assembly is read backwards
to stop means to plug a gap, so the work and admin letters go inside the belly word

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, and tum is a belly
op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of admin

explanation.surface: A firm in a downturn plans work with an admin chief to halt the slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old jocular British word for a pot belly, not a company; 'in recession' reverses the whole assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay out a course in detail, as a route on a chart, is to plan it; the phrasal verb is a synonym.

clue.text: 6 pupils regularly filling in petition

definitions.note: the cross-reference sends the solver to the answer at 6 down, meaning compliant

indicators.note: filling in means sitting inside, so the picked letters go within the petition word

parts.note: to sue is to petition or appeal, as in suing for peace

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter, here the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Six schoolchildren take turns completing a petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes PPL from PuPiLs, 'filling in' SUE. The 6 is not a number but the 6 down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexible and pliant, bending easily, matches the compliant answer at the cross-referenced light.

clue.text: Rifles thrust over cashiers

parts.note: ran, as in ran a sword through, means thrust
to cashier is to dismiss, so cashiers means sacks

explanation.surface: Guns pushed over bank tellers, as in a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifles' and 'cashiers' look like nouns but are verbs: searches roughly, dismisses.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search through something thoroughly to steal, so rifles is a synonym of searching and plundering.
